mainTopic: Leaving the meal (עקירה): רבי יהודה vs. the רבנן, רבי יוחנן's defense, and support for רב חסדא; then a meal interrupted by שבת
overview: Earlier, רב חסדא taught that foods whose after-ברכה must be said where they were eaten (like bread or wine) need no new ברכה if a person leaves and comes back. Other foods do need a new ברכה. The גמרא first shows that the ברייתא which seemed to contradict him is רבי יהודה's minority view. In that ברייתא, the תנא קמא says friends who step out to the בית הכנסת need no new ברכות, while רבי יהודה requires them if nobody stayed at the table. The גמרא reads the רבנן as lenient only for foods needing their after-ברכה in place, and suggests this is another refutation of רבי יוחנן, who holds that changing location never requires a new ברכה. But רבי יוחנן can answer: the ברייתא picked this case only to show how strict רבי יהודה is, so the רבנן may be lenient for all foods. Next, a ברייתא about friends drinking wine who left and returned supports רב חסדא. Finally, the גמרא returns to a meal interrupted when שבת begins. רבי יהודה says to stop for קידוש and ברכת המזון over two cups, and רבי יוסי says one may keep eating. The analysis of that dispute continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who holds that leaving the meal requires new blessings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the view that getting up and leaving a meal (עקירה) requires new ברכות, even for foods that need their after-ברכה in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who taught that 'uprooting' (getting up and leaving the meal) requires new blessings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the author is of the opinion that getting up from a meal means you must make new ברכות. It is setting up its next move, which is to show that this is only one תנא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier ברייתא seemed to contradict רב חסדא's rule that foods needing their after-ברכה in place do not need a new ברכה after leaving. רב נחמן בר יצחק answered that this ברייתא is only רבי יהודה's view. This question opens the proof for that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (the author of this opinion)?
'Uprootings': getting up and leaving the place of the meal

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who taught about 'uprootings' (that leaving requires new blessings)?
phrases.notes: Refers to the ברייתא that challenged רב חסדא earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by continuing the defense of רב חסדא from the previous discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who requires new ברכות after leaving the meal.

steps.title: רבי יהודה, as shown by a ברייתא about friends who leave
steps.stepSummary: The answer is רבי יהודה. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא whose first opinion (the תנא קמא) says that friends who leave the meal for the בית הכנסת or בית המדרש need no new ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: friends who were reclining at a meal got up to go to the synagogue or the study hall. When they leave, they do not need to say an after-blessing for what they ate. When they come back, they do not need to make a new blessing before they eat again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the strict view belongs to רבי יהודה. It begins quoting the ברייתא that proves this, starting with the lenient first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא treats stepping out briefly as a pause, not as the end of the meal. So no after-ברכה is said on leaving, and no new first ברכה is said on returning. This lenient opinion is the majority view (the רבנן), and it matches רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Friends; a group eating together
Reclining (eating a formal meal)
Retroactively; here, the after-ברכה on what was already eaten
At the start; here, a new opening ברכה before eating again

steps.confusionAlert: 'ברכה למפרע' here does not mean anything mysterious. It simply means the after-ברכה (like ברכת המזון) for the food eaten before leaving. 'ברכה לכתחלה' means the first ברכה before starting to eat again.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda, as it was taught in a baraita:
Friends who were reclining at a meal,
and they got up (literally, 'uprooted their feet') to go
to the synagogue or to the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהֵן יוֹצְאִין — אֵין טְעוּנִין בְּרָכָה לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: when they leave, they do not need an after-blessing for what they ate,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁהֵן חוֹזְרִין — אֵין טְעוּנִין בְּרָכָה לְכַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.english: and when they return, they do not need a new opening blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 and brings the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The strict view is רבי יהודה's, a minority opinion in a ברייתא. The תנא קמא is lenient.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires new blessings if nobody stayed behind
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the leniency to a case where some friends stayed at the table. If everyone left, they need an after-ברכה when they leave and a new ברכה when they return.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this rule apply? When they left some of the friends behind at the meal. But if they did not leave any friends there, then when they leave they need an after-blessing, and when they return they need a new opening blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the ברייתא. It proves that the strict view, requiring new ברכות after leaving, belongs to רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the meal continues only if someone keeps it going at the table. If everyone walks out, the meal has ended. Since this strictness is רבי יהודה's minority view, רב חסדא can follow the majority (the רבנן) without contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: When does this rule apply? (introduces a limitation)
Some; part of the group
They require a ברכה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the challenge against רב חסדא came from a minority opinion. That rescues his position.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
When is this statement said?
When they left some of the friends there at the meal,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא הִנִּיחוּ שָׁם מִקְצָת חֲבֵרִים,
phrases.english: but if they did not leave some of the friends there,
when they leave, they need an after-blessing for what they ate,
and when they return, they need a new opening blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 2 and supplies the actual proof.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the strict view on עקירה is רבי יהודה's alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of חברים שהיו מסובין, with רבי יהודה's limitation.

steps.title: Reading the רבנן's view: their leniency is only for foods needing an after-ברכה in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that the רבנן are lenient only for foods whose after-ברכה must be said in place. For other foods, even the רבנן require new ברכות after leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the reason for the רבנן's leniency is that they are talking about foods that need their after-blessing said in their place. That is why, when people leave, they do not need an after-blessing, and when they return, they do not need a new opening blessing. But for foods that do not need their after-blessing said in their place, even the רבנן agree: when people leave, they need an after-blessing, and when they return, they need a new opening blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the רבנן's lenient view by narrowing it. This narrowing sets up the next move, a challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The friends in the ברייתא were eating a meal with bread, which needs its after-ברכה at the place of eating. So when they return, they are still tied to that meal. Foods without this requirement have no such tie, so leaving ends them, even according to the רבנן. This fits רב חסדא's split rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, the reason is (introduces an inference about the reason)
In their place; the after-ברכה must be said where the food was eaten
After them; the after-ברכה
According to the רבנן (the majority sages)

steps.confusionAlert: The רבנן are not lenient about every food. The גמרא is saying their leniency covers only foods that need their after-ברכה said in place.

phrases.english: But the reason is
that with foods that require a blessing after them in their place,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְשֶׁהֵן יוֹצְאִין — אֵין טְעוּנִין בְּרָכָה לְמַפְרֵעַ,
phrases.english: that is why, when they leave, they do not need an after-blessing,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁהֵן חוֹזְרִין — אֵין טְעוּנִין בְּרָכָה לְכַתְּחִלָּה.
phrases.english: and when they return, they do not need an opening blessing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין טְעוּנִין בְּרָכָה לְאַחֲרֵיהֶן בִּמְקוֹמָן,
phrases.english: But foods that do not require a blessing after them in their place,
even according to the Rabbis,
when they leave, they need an after-blessing,
and when they return, they need an opening blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּבִדְבָרִים הַטְּעוּנִין בְּרָכָה לְאַחֲרֵיהֶן בִּמְקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the רבנן's side of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to the רבנן, foods that do not need their after-ברכה in place require new ברכות after leaving.

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this inference refutes רבי יוחנן, who holds that a change of location never requires a new ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the inference from step 4 to attack רבי יוחנן's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that changing location never requires a new ברכה, for any food. But the inference shows that everyone, even the רבנן, requires new ברכות for foods that do not need their after-ברכה in place. If no תנא agrees with רבי יוחנן, his view seems refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say?
A conclusive refutation
The אמורא who holds that a change of location never requires a new ברכה

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a conclusive refutation of Rabbi Yochanan?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the inference of step 4 against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that a change of location never requires a new ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the lenient רבנן require new ברכות for foods that do not need their after-ברכה in place. So no תנא supports רבי יוחנן's blanket leniency.

steps.title: Wasn't רבי יוחנן already refuted once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion: רבי יוחנן was already refuted earlier, so why bring another refutation?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we already refute him once?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether a second refutation is needed, since רבי יוחנן's view was already disproved earlier in the סוגיא. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, רבי יוחנן was already shown to be wrong. Refuting a view that has already fallen seems pointless. So the גמרא asks why it should bother.

keyTerms.meaning: We refuted him
One time

phrases.english: But didn't we already refute him once?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the refutation proposed in step 5 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The usefulness of bringing a new refutation of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view that was already disproved does not need another refutation.

steps.title: Let this be one more refutation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רבי יוחנן was already refuted, but says this ברייתא counts as an additional refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that this is also a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a second refutation is still worth stating, so it proposes this ברייתא as one more proof against רבי יוחנן. The next step shows that רבי יוחנן can defend himself against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא accepts that רבי יוחנן was already refuted once, but says it is still worth asking whether this ברייתא also refutes him. This is only a proposal, built entirely on the inference of step 4. The next step shows that רבי יוחנן can answer it, so this ברייתא is not a conclusive refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: From this one too
Let us say

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא only proposes reading the רבנן as lenient just for foods that need their after-ברכה in place, which would make this ברייתא another refutation of רבי יוחנן. The next step shows that רבי יוחנן can answer this, so the ברייתא does not refute him.

phrases.english: Let us say that from this one too there is a refutation!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession with addition: the earlier refutation stands, and this source is added to it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוחנן was already refuted, there would be no point in another refutation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is proposed as an additional refutation of רבי יוחנן. Step 8 rejects this proposal.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's defense: the wording shows the strength of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן can say the רבנן are lenient for all foods. The phrase 'they uprooted their feet' was used only to show how far רבי יהודה's stringency reaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can answer you: the same is true even for foods that do not need an after-ברכה in their place. They also need no new ברכה. The ברייתא said 'they uprooted their feet' only to show you how strong רבי יהודה's view is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the refutation of רבי יוחנן from Steps 4–7. It shows that the ברייתא can be read in a way that fits him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The refutation depended on an inference: since the case involves foods that need an after-ברכה in place, the רבנן must be lenient only for those foods. רבי יוחנן answers that the case was chosen for another reason, to highlight רבי יהודה. So the רבנן could be lenient for every food, which matches רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: "He can say to you": introduces how a challenged אמורא would defend himself
The same law applies (to another case as well)
"To inform you of the strength": a detail added to show how far someone's opinion goes
They uprooted their feet, meaning they got up and left the place of eating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רבי יוחנן agreeing with רבי יהודה. He is only explaining why the ברייתא picked this particular case. His own view still follows the רבנן, read as lenient for all foods.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan can say to you:
the same law applies, that even
foods that do not require a blessing
afterward in their place
also do not need to recite a new blessing;
and that which it teaches, "they uprooted their feet,"
phrases.notes: These are the exact words the earlier argument was based on.

phrases.english: is to inform you of the strength of Rabbi Yehuda's view,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the refutation of רבי יוחנן proposed in Steps 5–7 by reinterpreting the wording it relied on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from Step 4 that the רבנן are lenient only for foods needing an after-ברכה in place.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference assumed the case detail limits the רבנן. In fact it was chosen to show the strength of רבי יהודה's stringency.

steps.title: Explaining how this case shows רבי יהודה's strength
steps.stepSummary: Even for foods needing an after-ברכה in place, where people will surely come back, רבי יהודה is lenient only if some friends stayed. Otherwise he requires an after-ברכה on leaving and a new ברכה on returning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even for foods that need an after-ברכה in their place, רבי יהודה's only reason to be lenient is that some friends stayed behind. If no friends stayed, then when they leave they must say an after-ברכה, and when they come back they must say a new opening ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what 'the strength of רבי יהודה' means. It shows why the ברייתא chose this particular case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Foods that need an after-ברכה in place almost force the eater to come back, so you might think leaving does not break the meal. רבי יהודה is strict even here unless friends stayed. That stringency is the 'strength' the ברייתא wanted to show, so the case teaches nothing about limiting the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: They left some of their friends behind at the table
Retroactively, here meaning the after-ברכה for what was already eaten
From the start, here meaning a new opening ברכה before eating again
The reason (often implying: only for this reason, but not otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's position survives. The ברייתא's case was chosen to show רבי יהודה's stringency, not to limit the רבנן's leniency.

phrases.english: that even foods which require a blessing
afterward in their place,
the reason is only that they left some friends behind;
but if they did not leave some friends behind,
when they go out, they require a blessing afterward (for what they ate),
and when they return, they require a new opening blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲפִילּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁטְּעוּנִין בְּרָכָה לְאַחֲרֵיהֶן בִּמְקוֹמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase 'to inform you of the strength of רבי יהודה' from Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting why a case detail appears in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'they uprooted their feet' with in-place foods shows the רבנן are lenient only for such foods.
steps.terutzMaskana: The detail shows that רבי יהודה is strict even in the strongest case for leniency. The רבנן may be lenient for all foods.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רב חסדא: wine drinkers who leave and return
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that friends drinking wine who left and came back do not need a new ברכה. This matches רב חסדא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that supports רב חסדא: friends who were reclining to drink wine, then got up and came back, do not need to say a new ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that backs up רב חסדא's view from earlier in the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is a food that needs its after-ברכה in the place where it was drunk. רב חסדא ruled that with such foods, leaving and returning does not require a new ברכה. This ברייתא says exactly that, so it is clear support for him.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was taught in accordance with him": a ברייתא supports this אמורא
Reclining together at a meal, sitting as a group
Wine, a drink that requires its after-ברכה in its place

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב חסדא's middle position (no new ברכה only for foods needing an after-ברכה in place) has direct ברייתא support.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Chisda:
friends who were reclining to drink wine,
and they uprooted their feet and returned,
do not need to recite a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רבי יוחנן, the גמרא adds direct support for רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that foods needing an after-ברכה in place need no new ברכה after leaving and returning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about friends drinking wine who left and returned.

steps.title: A meal interrupted by the arrival of שבת: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: when שבת begins during a group meal, רבי יהודה says they say קידוש over one cup and ברכת המזון over a second. רבי יוסי says one may keep eating until dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if a group was reclining at a meal and the day became holy (שבת began), they bring him a cup of wine and he says קידוש over it, and over a second cup he says ברכת המזון. This is רבי יהודה's view. רבי יוסי says: he may keep eating until it gets dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches back to an earlier topic, a meal interrupted by שבת. It brings a ברייתא with a dispute that the following discussion will analyze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that once שבת arrives, the meal must stop for קידוש, and he uses two separate cups, one for קידוש and one for ברכת המזון. רבי יוסי holds that a meal that started before שבת is not interrupted, so one may continue eating. This dispute sets the base for the coming discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Sages taught": introduces a ברייתא
Members of a group eating together
The day became holy for them, meaning שבת or יום טוב began during the meal
The sanctification of the day, i.e. קידוש
Grace after meals
He continues eating without stopping

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. It is no longer about leaving the table. It is about whether the arrival of שבת forces a meal to stop.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
members of a group who were reclining (at a meal)
and the day became sanctified for them,
they bring him a cup of wine
and he recites over it the sanctification of the day (קידוש),
and over a second cup he recites Grace after Meals;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:
he continues eating until it gets dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה שֶׁהָיוּ מְסוּבִּין וְקִדֵּשׁ עֲלֵיהֶן הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of changing location and returns to the earlier subject of interrupting a meal for קידוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: when שבת arrives, stop and say קידוש over one cup and ברכת המזון over a second. רבי יוסי: the meal may continue without interruption.
